LESSON: CONVERSATION

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.5: Conversation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Conversation. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. ask and answer relevant questions in a listening text
2. build on the ideas and points of others in conversation by linking their comments to those of others.
3. increase the vocabulary range through focused listening and understanding of general and specific details e) demonstrate respect for others when participating in a conversation 153 f) appreciate the use of socially acceptable language and mannerisms in conversation follow-up conversation.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. ask and answer relevant questions in a listening text
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to ask and answer relevant questions in a listening text. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. build on the ideas and points of others in conversation by linking their comments to those of others.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to build on the ideas and points of others in conversation by linking their comments to those of others. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. increase the vocabulary range through focused listening and understanding of general and specific details e) demonstrate respect for others when participating in a conversation 153 f) appreciate the use of socially acceptable language and mannerisms in conversation follow-up conversation.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to increase the vocabulary range through focused listening and understanding of general and specific details e) demonstrate respect for others when participating in a conversation 153 f) appreciate the use of socially acceptable language and mannerisms in conversation follow-up conversation. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Conversation using something you see at school.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Conversation.
2. Explain Conversation to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Conversation.
4. Show that you can: ask and answer relevant questions in a listening text
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Conversation. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Conversation important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. ask and answer relevant questions in a listening text
2. build on the ideas and points of others in conversation by linking their comments to those of others.
3. increase the vocabulary range through focused listening and understanding of general and specific details e) demonstrate respect for others when participating in a conversation 153 f) appreciate the use of socially acceptable language and mannerisms in conversation follow-up conversation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
